content.title: About
content.content: Coconut is the fruit of the coconut palm (Cocos nucifera), cultivated in tropical regions worldwide. The packaged product contains whole coconuts that have been stripped of the outer fibrous husk but retain the inner flesh and coconut water. The nuts have a distinctive aroma, a mildly sweet taste, and a dense yet tender texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The coconut palm is often called the “tree of life” in many tropical cultures.
Coconut water is a natural isotonic drink rich in electrolytes.
Coconut flesh contains about 30 % saturated fat, mainly lauric acid.
Coconut oil is extracted from dried flesh (copra) by cold pressing.
Whole coconuts can float in water for up to nine days thanks to their hollow interior.

items.title: Rich in electrolytes
items.content: Coconut water provides potassium, sodium, magnesium, and calcium, helping maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Source of lauric acid
items.content: Lauric acid exhibits antibacterial and antiviral properties.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Compounds from coconut flesh may help lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Antioxidant effect
items.content: Coconut contains phenolic compounds that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The fiber in the flesh promotes intestinal motility and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to coconut products.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive consumption of coconut flesh or oil can increase overall saturated fat intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Coconut flesh and oil are energy‑dense; portion sizes should be moderated.

items.title: Copper content
items.content: Large amounts of coconut may lead to excess copper in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Packaged coconut can be eaten fresh as a snack, added to smoothies, yogurt, salads, or baked goods. The flesh is cut into cubes, and the coconut water is enjoyed chilled or used as a base for sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store whole coconuts in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, keep the flesh in an airtight container in the refrigerator and consume within 3–5 days. Coconut water should be refrigerated and used within 2 days.
